claim: EAATs regulate glutamatergic signaling by mediating the clearance of extracellular glutamate from the synapse into neuronal and glial cells.
source: Excitatory amino acid transporters (EAATs) regulate glutamatergic signaling by mediating the clearance of extracellular (EC) glutamate from the synapse into neuronal and glial cells (Danbolt, 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Danbolt, 2001, which is a reference to established scientific literature.

claim: EAATs couple the influx of three sodium ions and one proton and the efflux of one potassium ion to the inward translocation of one glutamate molecule.
source: EAATs accomplish this task through a secondary active transport mechanism that couples the influx of three sodium ions and one proton and the efflux of one potassium ion to the inward translocation of one glutamate molecule (Levy et al., 1998; Zerangue and Kavanaugh, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Levy et al., 1998 and Zerangue and Kavanaugh, 1996.

claim: EAATs mediate a thermodynamically uncoupled substrate-gated chloride conductance.
source: In addition, they mediate a thermodynamically uncoupled substrate-gated chloride conductance (Fairman et al., 1995; Wadiche et al., 1995), which modulates cell excitability serving as a sensor of EC glutamate concentrations (Melzer et al., 2005; Veruki et al., 2006; Wersinger et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fairman et al., 1995; Wadiche et al., 1995; Melzer et al., 2005; Veruki et al., 2006; Wersinger et al., 2006.

claim: EAATs display an evolutionarily conserved trimeric quaternary structure.
source: EAATs display an evolutionarily conserved trimeric quaternary structure (Gendreau et al., 2004; Haugeto et al., 1996; Yernool et al., 2003, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gendreau et al., 2004; Haugeto et al., 1996; Yernool et al., 2003, 2004.

claim: Each EAAT protomer contains eight transmembrane helices and two reentrant hairpin loops, HP1 and HP2.
source: Each protomer contains eight transmembrane (TM) helices and two reentrant hairpin loops, HP1 and HP2 (Yernool et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yernool et al., 2004.

claim: TM1, TM2, TM4 and TM5 make intersubunit contacts and form the trimerization domain.
source: TM1, TM2, TM4 and TM5 make intersubunit contacts and form the trimerization domain (Boudker et al., 2007; Lezon and Bahar, 2012; Reyes et al., 2009; Yernool et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Boudker et al., 2007; Lezon and Bahar, 2012; Reyes et al., 2009; Yernool et al., 2004.

claim: The transport domain composed of HP1, HP2, TM7, TM8, TM3 and TM6 moves in an elevator-like motion across the membrane to enable substrate translocation.
source: These core elements, together with TM3 and TM6, form the transport domain that moves in an elevator-like motion across the membrane to enable substrate translocation (Lezon and Bahar, 2012; Reyes et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lezon and Bahar, 2012; Reyes et al., 2009.

claim: GltPh has been crystallized in outward-facing state (OFS) and inward-facing state (IFS).
source: GltPh has been crystallized in two end-states: outward-facing state (OFS) (Boudker et al., 2007; Yernool et al., 2004) and inward-facing state (IFS) (Reyes et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Boudker et al., 2007; Yernool et al., 2004; Reyes et al., 2009.

claim: Verdon and Boudker identified an asymmetric intermediate state where one of the protomers was in an intermediate outward-facing state (iOFS) and two others in IFS.
source: Moreover, Verdon and Boudker identified an asymmetric intermediate state where one of the protomers was in an intermediate outward-facing state (iOFS) and two others in IFS (Verdon and Boudker, 2012) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Verdon and Boudker, 2012 and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The asymmetric GltPh crystal structure closely resembles an earlier prediction that GltPh is likely to sample intermediate conformations with 'mixed' states of the subunits.
source: Strikingly, this crystal structure closely resembles our earlier prediction (Jiang et al., 2011), which suggested that GltPh is likely to sample intermediate conformations, with 'mixed' states of the subunits.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jiang et al., 2011.

claim: Residues in TM2 are involved in anion conduction.
source: An initial effort to define regions in EAATs involved in anion flux identified residues in TM2 (Ryan et al., 2004) that, when mutated, affected anion conduction, implicating this region in anion permeation.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ryan et al., 2004.

claim: Additional residues in TM2, TM5, HP1 and TM7 contribute to chloride permeation and/or anion channel gating.
source: Additional residues in TM2 (Kovermann et al., 2010; Ryan and Mindell, 2007; Ryan et al., 2004; Winter et al., 2012), TM5, HP1 and TM7 (Cater et al., 2014; Huang and Vandenberg, 2007; Machtens et al., 2015; Torres-Salazar et al., 2015) also appear to contribute to chloride permeation and/or anion channel gating.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kovermann et al., 2010; Ryan and Mindell, 2007; Ryan et al., 2004; Winter et al., 2012; Cater et al., 2014; Huang and Vandenberg, 2007; Machtens et al., 2015; Torres-Salazar et al., 2015.

claim: The interface between the transport and trimerization domains could facilitate anion permeation.
source: EAAT1 residues in this cavity were tested by Cater et al. (2014), who suggested that the interface between the transport and trimerization domains could facilitate anion permeation (Cater et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cater et al., 2014.

claim: The formation of anion-selective permeation pathway is unlikely in the iOFS but required a global rearrangement including a lateral movement of the transport domain.
source: Recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by Fahlke's group (Machtens et al., 2015) showed that the formation of anion-selective permeation pathway is unlikely in the iOFS proposed earlier (Verdon and Boudker, 2012), but required a global rearrangement of the iOFS that included a lateral movement of the transport domain to facilitate the anion pore opening.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Machtens et al., 2015.

claim: A chloride-channeling intermediate state, iChS, is transiently accessible as EAAT1 reconfigures from substrate/ion-loaded into a substrate-releasing conformer.
source: Using a combination of molecular modeling, substituted cysteine accessibility, electrophysiology and glutamate uptake assays, we identified a chloride-channeling conformer, iChS, transiently accessible as EAAT1 reconfigures from substrate/ion-loaded into a substrate-releasing conformer.
evidence: The claim is supported by the combination of computational and experimental methods described in the manuscript.

claim: Opening of the anion permeation path in iChS is controlled by the elevator-like movement of the substrate-binding core and repacking of a cluster of hydrophobic residues near the extracellular vestibule.
source: Opening of the anion permeation path in this iChS is controlled by the elevator-like movement of the substrate-binding core, along with its wall that simultaneously lines the anion permeation path (global); and repacking of a cluster of hydrophobic residues near the extracellular vestibule (local).
evidence: The claim is supported by the computational and experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Stabilization of iChS by chemical modifications favors anion channeling at the expense of substrate transport.
source: Moreover, our results demonstrate that stabilization of iChS by chemical modifications favors anion channeling at the expense of substrate transport, suggesting a mutually exclusive regulation mediated by the movement of the flexible wall lining the two regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from chemical modification experiments.

claim: A water channel intermittently forms during transition of the substrate-loaded subunit from the iOFS to the IFS.
source: A water channel intermittently forms during transition of the substrate-loaded subunit from the iOFS to the IFS
evidence: This is a section heading that summarizes findings from the simulations described in the section.

claim: The pore radius near the constriction zone formed by M286, Y195, S65 and P304 was 0.9 ± 0.4 Å in the iOFS.
source: The pore radius near this constriction zone was 0.9 ± 0.4 Å, which would render the pore impermeable to chloride ions (1.8 Å in radius).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational measurements from MD simulations.

claim: M286 is separated from Y195 by over 15 Å in the IFS, which might easily accommodate an anion passage.
source: On the other hand, M286 (in HP1) is separated from Y195 by over 15 Å in the IFS, which might easily accommodate an anion passage.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural measurements from simulations.

claim: A water channel transiently formed in a region at the interface between the transport and trimerization domains during the transition from iOFS to IFS.
source: Instead, a water channel transiently formed in another (nearby) region at the interface between the transport and trimerization domains (encircled in Figure 1B), during the transition.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The hydrated channel was invariably observed in the presence of either two or three bound Na+ ions and the substrate (aspartate in GltPh).
source: The hydrated channel, was invariably observed in the presence of either two or three bound Na+ ions and the substrate (aspartate in GltPh) (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The iChS first showed a minimum pore radius of 1.6 ± 0.2 Å, which is not wide enough to allow for chloride permeation.
source: The iChS first showed a minimum pore radius of 1.6 ± 0.2 Å, which is not wide enough to allow for chloride permeation; but further equilibration with conventional MD (cMD) simulations in the presence of externally applied voltages (see Materials and methods) led to full occupancy of the channel by continuous water.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational measurements from MD simulations.

claim: The increase in water occupancy in the presence of an electric field may reflect the voltage-gating characteristics of the channel.
source: The increase in water occupancy in the presence of an electric field may reflect the voltage-gating characteristics of the channel (Machtens et al., 2015; Melzer et al., 2003, 2005).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by citations to Machtens et al., 2015; Melzer et al., 2003, 2005.

claim: The cluster of hydrophobic residues F50, V51 and L212 underwent a significant reconfiguration to give rise to a pore opening in the iChS.
source: In our simulations, the cluster of hydrophobic residues F50, V51 and L212 underwent a significant reconfiguration, to give rise to a pore opening in the iChS (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the iOFS and IFS, the region near F50, V51 and L212 was blocked by tight packing of the same residues.
source: In the iOFS and IFS, this particular region was blocked by tight packing of the same residues.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data.

claim: The opening of the water channel was enabled by the concerted downward movement of the two helical hairpins HP1 and HP2, together with the rotational isomerization of F50, V51 and L212 side chains.
source: The opening of the water channel was enabled by the concerted downward movement of the two helical hairpins HP1 and HP2, together with the rotational isomerization of F50, V51 and L212 side chains (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The minimum pore radius fluctuated around 2.3 ± 0.3 Å during the simulations, which is comparable to the value of 2.4 Å reported for the crystal structure of an open glutamate-gated chloride channel.
source: The minimum pore radius fluctuated around 2.3 ± 0.3 Å during the simulations, which is comparable to the value of 2.4 Å reported for the crystal structure of an open glutamate-gated chloride channel (Hibbs and Gouaux, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data and comparison to a citation (Hibbs and Gouaux, 2011).

claim: The occupancy of chloride was observed to enlarge the pore up to 2.6 ± 0.2 Å.
source: Whereas our minimum pore radius was calculated in the absence of chloride, the occupancy of chloride was observed to enlarge the pore up to 2.6 ± 0.2 Å, showing certain flexibility at this constriction to attain the experimentally-determined pore radii of >2.5 Å (Wadiche and Kavanaugh, 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data and comparison to experimental data (Wadiche and Kavanaugh, 1998).

claim: The chloride ion was detected to translocate across the channel in one of the runs, indicating that iChS conformer presents a pore permeable to chloride.
source: The chloride ion was detected to translocate across this channel in one of the runs, indicating that iChS conformer presents a pore permeable to chloride.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data.

claim: V51, L212, F50 and V209 showed a significantly higher SASA value in the iChS than in either the iOFS or the IFS.
source: On the EC side, V51, L212, F50 and V209 showed a significantly higher SASA value in the iChS than in either the iOFS or the IFS (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by SASA calculations shown in Figure 3A.

claim: F50 and V209 were almost completely buried in the IFS or the iOFS, and became solvent accessible only upon transition to the iChS.
source: In particular, F50 and V209 were almost completely buried in the IFS or the iOFS, and became solvent accessible only upon transition to the iChS.
evidence: The claim is supported by SASA calculations.

claim: Y195 showed a higher accessibility in the iChS when compared to IFS or iOFS.
source: On the IC side, Y195 showed a higher accessibility in the iChS when compared to IFS or iOFS.
evidence: The claim is supported by SASA calculations.

claim: Application of 10 mM MTSES decreased the anion current amplitude at +60 mV to 61.5 ± 5% with a time constant of 5.5 ± 0.5 s in oocytes expressing M89C.
source: In oocytes expressing M89C (V51 in GltPh), using a NO3--based solution to monitor the effect on the anion conductance, application of 10 mM MTSES decreased the anion current amplitude at +60 mV to 61.5 ± 5% with a time constant of 5.5 ± 0.5 s (n = 6) (Figure 3C and D), an effect that was reversed by the application of 1 mM 1,4-Dithiothreitol (DTT) (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The reduction in current amplitude by MTSES in M89C occurred at positive potentials, suggesting that only the anion conductance was affected and that substrate transport remained intact.
source: This reduction in current amplitude occurred at positive potentials, suggesting that only the anion conductance was affected and that substrate transport, which is predominant at negative potentials, remained intact (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transport current in cells expressing M89C remained intact after application of MTSES.
source: In contrast to the anion current, the transport current in cells expressing M89C remained intact after application of MTSES (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The uptake of radiolabeled glutamate was not affected by application of 10 mM MTSES to oocytes expressing M89C.
source: Moreover, the uptake of radiolabeled glutamate was not affected by application of 10 mM MTSES to oocytes expressing M89C (Figure 3E, n > 15).
evidence: The claim is supported by uptake assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: MTSET and MTSACE produced a similar decrease in the anion current without altering substrate translocation in M89C.
source: Both reagents produced a similar decrease in the anion current without altering substrate translocation (Figure 3F–K, n > 3), further confirming that M89C is accessible to thiol-specific reagents and, that the resulting modifications decrease anion permeation without affecting substrate translocation.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological and uptake data shown in Figure 3F–K.

claim: Application of 10 mM MTSES to cells expressing L296C reduced the NO3−-mediated current at +60 mV to 59 ± 8.9% with a time constant of 15.6 ± 0.5 s.
source: Application of 10 mM MTSES to cells expressing L296C also reduced the NO3−-mediated current at +60 mV to 59 ± 8.9% (n > 5) with a time constant of 15.6 ± 0.5 s (Figure 3L–M), which was reversible by DTT (Figure 3M) and did not affect glutamate uptake (Figure 3N).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 3L–M.

claim: MTSACE reduced the anion current without altering substrate transport in L296C.
source: MTSACE also reduced the anion current without altering substrate transport (Figure 3O–Q, n > 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological and uptake data shown in Figure 3O–Q.

claim: L88 in hEAAT1 showed the most dramatic change in its SASA between the iOFS or IFS and iChS.
source: Notably, our SASA calculations revealed that at least in hEAAT1, L88 was the residue that showed the most dramatic change in its SASA between the iOFS or IFS and iChS (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by SASA calculations shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the IFS and iOFS, the SASA for L88 was less than 10 Å2, while in the iChS, it became 60 ± 20 Å2.
source: In the IFS and iOFS, the SASA for L88 was less than 10 Å2, while in the iChS, it became 60 ± 20 Å2 (comparable to that of M89 and L296).
evidence: The claim is supported by SASA calculations.

claim: Oocytes expressing L88C did not show any significant changes in current amplitudes or substrate transport upon application of 10 mM MTSES or 1 mM MTSET.
source: In contrast to oocytes expressing M89C or L296C, the oocytes expressing L88C did not show any significant changes in current amplitudes or substrate transport upon application of 10 mM MTSES or 1 mM MTSET (Figure 4A–B,D–E and I), suggesting that L88 was not accessible from the EC side of the membrane.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological and uptake data shown in Figure 4A–B,D–E and I.

claim: Application of 2.5 mM MTSEA resulted in a slow increase in the anion current amplitude at +60 mV in oocytes expressing L88C, reaching a maximum of 10-fold increase within ~50 s.
source: Application of 2.5 mM MTSEA resulted in a slow increase in the anion current amplitude at +60 mV. About 10 s after the application, the current started increasing, to reach a maximum of 10-fold increase within ~50 s (Figure 4C, open circles, n = 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: No detectable changes were observed in oocytes-expressing Csls WT 50 s after an identical application of MTSEA.
source: No detectable changes were observed in oocytes-expressing Csls WT 50 s after an identical application of MTSEA (Figure 4C; gray triangles, n = 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The effect of MTSEA remains unchanged when applied after a previous application of MTSES or MTSET in L88C, indicating that L88C was not accessible to MTSES or MTSET.
source: Figure 4G and H (n > 3) show that the effect of MTSEA remains unchanged when applied after a previous application of the other reagents, indicating that L88C was not accessible to MTSES or MTSET.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: The lack of reactivity of L88C to membrane impermeable reagents suggests that L88C is deep in the anion pore and probably accessible only from the IC side.
source: The lack of reactivity of L88C to membrane impermeable reagents suggests that L88C is deep in the anion pore and probably accessible only from the IC side.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: Modification of L88C with MTSEA not only increased macroscopic anion currents but also significantly decreased substrate transport.
source: Interestingly, modification of L88C with MTSEA not only increased macroscopic anion currents but also significantly decreased substrate transport. Radiolabeled glutamate uptake was reduced more than 60% after incubation with 2.5 mM MTSEA (Figure 4I), the same conditions that resulted in a 10-fold increase of anion current.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological and uptake data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: L88 may be part of the permeation pathway and also involved in anion channel gating.
source: Therefore, these results suggest that L88 may be part of the permeation pathway, but it is also involved in anion channel gating.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: In oocytes-expressing L88R, macroscopic current amplitudes were much larger, with an increase of more than 10-fold when normalized by surface expression.
source: Similar to that observed after the modification with MTSEA, in oocytes-expressing L88R, we observed much larger macroscopic current amplitudes. The increase was more than 10-fold when normalized by surface expression (Figure 4K, n > 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: L88R showed less than 90% of substrate transport activity when compared with WT.
source: Moreover, L88R showed less than 90% of substrate transport activity when compared with WT (Figure 4L, n > 20).
evidence: The claim is supported by uptake data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: The permeability ratios to chloride in oocytes expressing the mutant L88R were significantly higher for all permeant anions when compared to the WT permeability ratios.
source: As shown in Figure 4M, the permeability ratios to chloride in oocytes expressing the mutant L88R were significantly higher for all permeant anions when compared to the WT permeability ratios, demonstrating that L88 may also be playing a role in anion selectivity.
evidence: The claim is supported by permeability ratio data shown in Figure 4M.

claim: The estimated energy barrier is ~4.0 kcal/mol as Cl− translocates through the hydrophobic constriction zone lined by F50, V51 and L212.
source: The estimated energy barrier is ~4.0 kcal/mol, as Cl− translocates through the hydrophobic constriction zone lined by F50, V51 and L212 (Figure 5C and Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by PMF calculations shown in Figure 5C and Video 2.

claim: R276 near the IC entrance plays a significant role in selectively permeating Cl− over Na+.
source: Notably, R276 near the IC entrance plays a significant role in selectively permeating Cl− over Na+ (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by PMF calculations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In the region near R276, Na+ ions encounter an energy barrier of 8.0 kcal/mol, indicating that the anion permeation path in the iChS is practically not accessible to Na+ ions.
source: In this region, Na+ ions encounter an energy barrier of 8.0 kcal/mol, indicating that the anion permeation path in the iChS is practically not accessible to Na+ ions.
evidence: The claim is supported by PMF calculations.

claim: The path lined by S65 remained obstructed by the hydrophobic residues V58, I61, V355, and A353, resulting in an energy barrier over 20 kcal/mol.
source: However, the path remained obstructed by the hydrophobic residues V58, I61, V355, and A353, resulting in an energy barrier over 20 kcal/mol (not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by metadynamics simulations.

claim: The path involving S65 is highly improbable to allow anion permeation, and S65 is not likely to direct the chloride ion to a permeable channel.
source: This result shows that this path is highly improbable to allow anion permeation, and S65 is not likely to direct the chloride ion to a permeable channel.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the simulation data.

claim: In oocytes-expressing S103C, no significant modification effect on the anion current was observed upon application of MTSET, MTSES or MTSEA.
source: Moreover, in oocytes-expressing S103C, we did not observe any significant modification effect on the anion current upon application of MTSET, MTSES or MTSEA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the simulations, the initial formation of the water channel occurred in a substrate-loaded state, in which the substrate-binding site was minimally hydrated and practically occluded to both EC and IC regions.
source: We note that in our simulations, the initial formation of the water channel occurred in a substrate-loaded state, in which the substrate-binding site was minimally hydrated and practically occluded to both EC and IC regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data.

claim: The opening of the channel is enabled by an 'elevator-like' displacement of the substrate-binding core and further enhanced by the applied voltage.
source: The opening of the channel (Figure 2) is enabled by an 'elevator-like' displacement of the substrate-binding core (Video 1) and further enhanced by the applied voltage.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2 and Video 1.

claim: Several residues in HP1, HP2 and TM8 act as a flexible wall between the substrate-binding site and anion-channeling path.
source: Several residues in HP1, HP2 and TM8 act as a flexible wall (Figure 6) between the substrate-binding site and anion-channeling path.
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The downward movement of the substrate-loaded core and especially these residues that form the wall create a volume expansion in the adjoining interfacial region, leading to the emergence of a continuous channel.
source: The downward movement of the substrate-loaded core and especially these residues that form the wall create a volume expansion in the adjoining interfacial region, leading to the emergence of a continuous channel (Figure 6, and Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 6 and Video 2.

claim: The iChS exhibited RMSDs of 4.5 ± 0.5 Å and 3.2 ± 0.5 Å from the iOFS and IFS, respectively.
source: Furthermore, while the RMSD between iOFS and IFS is 7.3 Å, the iChS exhibited RMSDs of 4.5 ± 0.5 Å and 3.2 ± 0.5 Å from the iOFS and IFS, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by RMSD calculations from simulations.

claim: When MTS-reagents were applied in high K+ conditions, M89C became inaccessible.
source: When we measured the current amplitudes in NaNO3 + glutamate before (white bars) and after (black bars) the application of MTSES in high K+ conditions (Figure 8A, center bars, n = 5), we did not observe the 40% reduction of the current amplitudes obtained when the application was done in conditions that favored channel opening (Figures 3C and 8A right bars, n = 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Application of MTSEA in a KNO3-based solution did not prevent the modification of L88C, but its effect was much smaller than when MTSEA was applied in a NaNO3-based solution.
source: Although application of MTSEA in a KNO3-based solution did not prevent the modification (Figure 8B, central bars, n = 4), its effect was much smaller than the observed when MTSEA was applied in a NaNO3-based solution (Figures 4 and 8B, right bars, n = 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: In the presence of 200 µM TBOA, no effect of MTSEA was observed on L88C.
source: In the presence of 200 µM TBOA, no effect of MTSEA was observed (Figure 8C–D, n = 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 8C–D.

claim: Following the application in TBOA, application of MTSEA in the same conditions used before increased the current about 10-fold in L88C.
source: In the same cells, following the application in TBOA, we applied MTSEA in the same conditions used before (Figure 4) and the effect was very similar, increasing the current about 10-fold (Figure 8C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 8C–D.

claim: When the carrier is stabilized in an outward-facing conformation the accessibility of L88C from the cytoplasm is limited or abolished.
source: This result demonstrates very little or no modification at all in the presence of TBOA, supporting the hypothesis that when the carrier is stabilized in an outward-facing conformation the accessibility of L88C from the cytoplasm is limited or abolished, consistent with the constriction we observed in the IC region in a similar conformation (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data and simulation data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The anion-selective pathway is conserved in archaeal and mammalian EAATs.
source: Our results confirm that the anion-selective pathway is conserved in archaeal and mammalian EAATs and that it consists of a cavity between the transport and the trimerization domains (Cater et al., 2014; Machtens et al., 2015) that opens up upon structural rearrangements from iOFS out of the transport cycle (Machtens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the combined computational and experimental data, and citations to Cater et al., 2014; Machtens et al., 2015.

claim: The anion pore opening consists of a cavity that is distinct from the substrate translocation path.
source: Moreover, our work provides novel evidence that the anion pore opening consists of a cavity that is distinct from the substrate translocation path and suggest that both pathways are limited by a flexible wall, whose movement dictate whether that monomer exclusively facilitates anion permeation or substrate translocation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the combined computational and experimental data.

claim: Both substrate transport and anion permeation pathways are limited by a flexible wall, whose movement dictates whether that monomer exclusively facilitates anion permeation or substrate translocation.
source: Moreover, our work provides novel evidence that the anion pore opening consists of a cavity that is distinct from the substrate translocation path and suggest that both pathways are limited by a flexible wall, whose movement dictate whether that monomer exclusively facilitates anion permeation or substrate translocation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the combined computational and experimental data.

claim: The anion channel and substrate translocation pathways are mutually exclusive.
source: This underscores the idea that the channel and substrate translocation pathways are mutually exclusive.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the data showing the flexible wall between the two pathways.

claim: The constriction zones observed in the permeation pathway in the iOFS and the IFS explain why the continuous permeation pathway is only observed in the iChS.
source: Another interesting and novel observation is the constriction zones that we observed of the permeation pathway in the iOFS and the IFS, which explains why the continuous permeation pathway is only observed in the iChS (Figure 6B)(Machtens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 6B and citation to Machtens et al., 2015.

claim: S65 (S103) may play a significant role in anion permeation by contributing to the structural elements involved in channel opening and closing but not as part of the permeation pathway.
source: Taken together with the previous reports, our results suggest that S65 (S103) may play a significant role in anion permeation by contributing to the structural elements involved in channel opening and closing but not as part of the permeation pathway.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the combined simulation and experimental data.

claim: The same mechanism of anion pore opening is robustly shared by both the archaeal and mammalian transporters GltPh and EAAT1.
source: The same mechanism is robustly shared by both the archaeal and mammalian transporters GltPh and EAAT1, and confirmed by both experiments and simulations.
evidence: The claim is supported by the combined computational and experimental data for both GltPh and EAAT1.
